name: Research is key for reforming education

content.title: Research is key for reforming education
content.summary: Educational reform should be guided by research to make policies that can resolve issues facing the education system in Pakistan today.

media.alt: Research is key for reforming education

content.text: Educational reform should be guided by research to make policies that can resolve issues facing the education system in Pakistan today. This was concluded by Professor Anwar Ahmed Zai, Chairman, Board of Intermediate Education, Karachi, at a policy dialogue on Educational Policy Reform, held at Aga Khan University's Institute for Educational Development (AKU-IED). " Education in developing countries needs repositioning, envisioning, and reshaping to address the challenges of globalisation, a growing knowledge society and knowledge-based economy," said Professor Zai.

Supporting the importance of research, Dr Muhammad Memon, Director, AKU-IED, spoke about the various initiatives of the Institute to develop and build the professional capacity of teachers and head teachers and to facilitate a culture of research and scholarship in the country. "A shared moral purpose of change, innovation, humility, motivation, commitment, accountability and empowerment are the key values that can make a difference in improving the present landscape of education."

Dr William Doe, Provost, AKU emphasised that just as it is the government's responsibility to facilitate strategies for the implementation of reforms in education, civil society and educational institutions should also be responsible for enhancing their own knowledge on a continuing basis.

The dialogue, which was a follow-up of an international conference on the Status of Educational Reform in the Developing Countries (South Asia) organised by AKU-IED in April 2008, was attended by teacher educators, policy makers, educational planners, educational reformists and educational researchers. The event aimed to provide a platform for researchers, teacher educators and practitioners to share their research with each other, at a time when the National Education Policy is being finalised by the Ministry of Education.
